about: Shared contract fixtures for Codex agent sessions brokered by RAVIS. RAVIS owns them in ravis/tests/fixtures/; Clarvis keeps a byte-identical copy in src/test/fixtures/, held to codex-contract.sha256. Every value is a fixture value: no token, key or hash is real. Nothing here is built yet.

files.conventions.json: this file: transport, callers, headers, the error catalogue and the shared rules
files.codex-state.json: GET /api/v1/codex: state, allowance and running tasks
files.codex-admin.json: sign-in, sign-out, account confirmation, version acceptance, the file-rules re-test, NERVIS's control routes
files.openai-refusal.json: the 400 on /v1/chat/completions and /v1/embeddings, and the conditional /v1/models entry
files.agent-sessions.json: the relay's session routes and shapes
files.owner-stop.json: the stop-only owner route, the launcher's codex stop and NERVIS's Stop route
files.project-locks.json: the project lock routes both engines use
files.../lock-rule-cases.json: the shared lock rule's cases, implemented by RAVIS and Clarvis alike

transport.actions: JSON over loopback HTTP; Content-Type: application/json; the form content types are refused
transport.events: server-sent events on GET /api/v1/agent-sessions/{sid}/events; no WebSockets, which skip RAVIS's admission layer

content_rule: Nothing in these routes, in RAVIS's logs or audit, or in MEP events carries prompt text, approval text, commands, file contents or diffs, except the relay stream and snapshot sent to a session-token holder, which carry what the window must render.

callers.client.clarvis: a client credential of application clarvis: code-server windows through the launcher's environment, desktop VS Code through the file named in clarvis.ravis.credentialFile
callers.client.nervis: NERVIS's client credential, which its GET relay presents on every read of RAVIS's /api/v1/
callers.client.other: a client credential whose application is not in settings.agent_client_applications
callers.admin.launcher: the launcher's admin credential; NERVIS holds it for its control routes
callers.admin.owner_cli: the owner's command-line admin credential in .run/ravis-owner.token, used only by run.py codex stop and codex reprove, never given to NERVIS
callers.note: caller names the credential presented in Authorization; its value never appears in a fixture

Idempotency-Key.scope: per session or workspace root, per window_id from the body, per key: two windows never share a key
Idempotency-Key.same_key_same_body: the original response is replayed: a retried settle returns the settled view, a retried transfer the same token, a retried reissue-token the same new token
Idempotency-Key.resolution_before_replay: an answer checks the request's resolution before replaying across windows, so another window gets 409 REQUEST_ALREADY_RESOLVED, never someone else's 200

X-Agent-Session-Token.returned: once at creation, and by reissue-token
X-Agent-Session-Token.stored_by_ravis: its sha256 only, compared in constant time
X-Agent-Session-Token.missing_or_wrong: 404 AGENT_SESSION_NOT_FOUND, so a session's existence doesn't leak
X-Agent-Session-Token.kept_by_clarvis_in: ~/.local/share/clarvis/agent-sessions/<sha256(workspace root realpath)>.json; folder 0700, file 0600, written atomically, deleted when the session ends

X-Lock-Lease.format: lk_ followed by an opaque value

headers.Last-Event-ID: the event stream's resume cursor; ?after= is equivalent

X-Clarvis-Engines.sent_by: Clarvis 0.17.0 or later, on listModels to a loopback base URL

rules: Clients match on code and details; message wording is informative and may change.
request_id and trace_id differ per response; fixtures use placeholders.
RAVIS's OpenAI-compatible /v1 endpoints keep OpenAI's error shape (openai-refusal.json).
NERVIS's own refusals before forwarding keep NERVIS's shape (owner-stop.json).

AGENT_CLIENT_NOT_ALLOWED.where: every agent-session and project-lock route except owner-stop, GETs included

AGENT_SESSION_NOT_FOUND.where: any {sid} route with a missing or wrong session token; owner-stop with an unknown id

ATTACH_INSTEAD.where: takeover of a lock a Codex session holds: Codex sessions are attached, never taken over

CLAIM_INVALID.where: settle with a claim that is not the current one

CODEX_HASH_MISMATCH.where: accept-version for a sha256 that is not the installed binary

CODEX_NOT_AVAILABLE.where: sign-in while not_installed, not_available or runtime_down

CODEX_NOT_READY.where: session create and turns while Codex's state is not ready, including unproven file rules, a changed account and, since R4, a new Codex build waiting to run (reason codex_update_pending)

CODEX_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE.where: session create, transcript, a sign-in whose start timed out, and since R4 every agent-session and project-lock route while RAVIS is still reconciling after a restart

CODEX_RUN_IN_PROGRESS.where: sign-in, sign-out and reprove while a Codex turn is active or a settle is pending

CODEX_SESSION_LIMIT.where: session create above the live-session limit (default 3)

CODEX_SIGN_IN_PORT_BUSY.where: sign-in while ports 1455 and 1457 are both held

CODEX_UNTESTED_VERSION.where: sign-in while the installed binary is neither tested nor accepted

CODEX_VERSION_CHECK_FAILED.where: accept-version when any of acceptance checks 1-6 failed

CONFIRMATION_MISMATCH.where: owner-stop (409); lock takeover (422) whose confirmation does not match, whose workspace_root isn't the lock's own root, or whose lock id is unknown

DECISION_NOT_ALLOWED.where: answer with a decision outside the request's allowed_decisions

EVENT_CURSOR_EXPIRED.where: events with a cursor older than the kept non-delta events, answered before streaming

FORBIDDEN.where: the Codex admin routes for a caller without an admin credential (RAVIS's existing code)

GIT_DIR_NOT_ALLOWED.where: session create and lock create whose git_dir fails the git-folder rule

HOLDER_ACTIVE.where: takeover of a Clarvis-engine run that is alive and working

IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED.where: a route that requires Idempotency-Key, called without one

IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED.where: the same Idempotency-Key with a different body

INVALID_REQUEST_BODY.where: a Codex admin route (sign-in, sign-out, account/confirm, accept-version, reprove), or since R3 an agent-session route and since R4 a project-lock route, whose body is not a JSON object, lacks a field the route needs, or names a value the route doesn't take (a mode, a turn kind, a settle next, a transfer's to); and a lock heartbeat, release or transfer without X-Lock-Lease

LEASE_REVOKED.where: heartbeat, release or transfer with a lease that no longer holds the lock: taken over, released, moved to the other engine, or never valid

LOCK_SUPERSEDED.where: turns, settle-claim and a resuming create while RAVIS's lock row is superseded after a restart

LOCK_TRANSFER_INVALID.where: session create, turns and lock create with a transfer token that is unknown, expired or for another root

NESTED_PROJECT_LOCKED.where: session create, turns and lock create when an ancestor or descendant root is locked

NOTHING_RUNNING.where: owner-stop on a session that is idle, stopped, paused, completed_needs_review or ended

NOTHING_TO_SETTLE.where: settle-claim on a session that needs no settle

NO_LEFTOVER.where: leftover when no leftover processes are recorded

OWNER_STOP_NOT_ALLOWED.where: owner-stop from anonymous, any client credential, or an admin application not in agent_owner_stop_applications

PROCESSES_NOT_CONFIRMED_GONE.where: settle-claim, settle, lock release, lock transfer and lock takeover before the holder's processes are confirmed gone (a takeover's details name them as leftover)

PROJECT_LOCKED.where: session create, turns, steer and lock create while another holder has the root

RATE_LIMITED.where: owner-stop above 10 calls a minute per application (RAVIS's existing code)

REPROOF_NOT_ALLOWED.where: reprove from any caller but an admin application in codex_reproof_applications (default owner_cli)

REQUEST_ALREADY_RESOLVED.where: answer to a request another window, Stop, the policy or the turn's end already resolved

REQUEST_NOT_FOUND.where: answer to an unknown request id

SESSION_STOPPING.where: turns, steer and answer once the session is stopping

SETTLE_CLAIMED.where: settle-claim while another window holds the claim

SETTLE_FIRST.where: turns and DELETE on a session that still needs a settle

SITE_NOT_ADDED.where: answer allow_site when Codex didn't add the site to its allowlist (it answered okOverridden, refused or didn't answer, or the host isn't a plain public host name); the site stays blocked and the request open

SIGN_IN_METHOD_NOT_SUPPORTED.where: sign-in with a method other than browser

TURN_ACTIVE.where: turns (steer instead) and DELETE while a turn is active

WINDOW_ATTACHED.where: reissue-token while a window attached within the last 60 s

WORKSPACE_ROOT_NOT_ALLOWED.where: session create and list, lock create and read, for a root outside the rule

identity_rule.dependency: require_agent_client(request), run first on every agent-session and project-lock route, GETs included

refusals_in_order.when: identity.may_write_configuration: any admin credential, including NERVIS's admin.launcher
refusals_in_order.message: Administrative credentials may not start, read, steer, stop or answer Codex tasks.

rules: The refusals run before the session token is examined, so a NERVIS credential holding a valid token is still refused.
Attributes are read directly, never through getattr(identity, name, False).
The one exception is POST /api/v1/agent-sessions/{sid}/owner-stop, on its own router with require_owner_stop_caller (owner-stop.json).
A route-table test fails if any other agent-session or project-lock route lacks require_agent_client, if owner-stop has it, or if reprove or the calibration route lacks require_owner_cli.

workspace_root_rule.accepted: the realpath of an existing directory inside one of settings.agent_allowed_roots (default ["~/Documents/coding"]; the launcher appends extras)
refused: an agent_allowed_roots entry itself, such as ~/Documents/coding
a folder that is, contains or lies inside a protected repository, or contains a denied path, unless that exact folder is listed in agent_allowed_roots with allow_protected: true

details_reason_fixed.protected_repository: is, contains or lies inside NERVIS-ecosystem or clarvis

workspace_root_rule.details_reason_other: RAVIS's relay increment (R3) adds: not_a_folder (missing or not a folder), home (the home folder itself), private_folder (inside ~/.config, ~/.local/share, ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/Library or ~/.codex), outside_allowed_roots, denied_path (is, holds or lies inside a denied path such as .run), lock_file_unwritable (the checkout lock file couldn't be written)
workspace_root_rule.protected_repositories_default: RAVIS's own checkout and its sibling clarvis, even when RAVIS starts without the launcher
workspace_root_rule.owner_decision: the ecosystem's own repositories stay refused; allowing one later needs an exact allow_protected listing and calibration K5c proving deny beats write inside a root
workspace_root_rule.binding: a session stores the realpath, and no later call can change it

git_dir_rule: <root>/.git is a directory and git_dir is its realpath; or
<root>/.git is a file reading 'gitdir: <path>', that path resolves to <main>/.git/worktrees/<name>, and that folder's gitdir file points back to <root>/.git.

serialised_routes.rule: one per-session action lock; presence is not serialised; interrupt, cancel and owner-stop set stopping inside the lock, before any answer that arrived at the same moment can be forwarded to Codex

applies_to: a steer that finds no active turn
a queued steer about to start its follow-on turn
turns_need_the_project_lock.holds_when: RAVIS's lock row names this session and is not superseded, and the checkout lock file names RAVIS
taken_atomically_when: the request carries lock.transfer_token (a switch back)
nothing holds the root or a nested root: the lock and the checkout lock file are created as create does
turns_need_the_project_lock.otherwise: 409 PROJECT_LOCKED {lock}, or NESTED_PROJECT_LOCKED, LOCK_SUPERSEDED or LOCK_TRANSFER_INVALID, and nothing starts
turns_need_the_project_lock.queued_steer_without_the_lock: starts nothing; RAVIS emits feedback {text, how: not_delivered}, and Clarvis keeps the text in the checkpoint's latestFeedback

open_points: Decided by RAVIS's relay increment (R3): a replayed create or reissue-token returns the original token within the same RAVIS run, where it is kept in memory beside the record for its 24 hours and never written to disk. After a RAVIS restart the token is gone, so the replay is answered as reissue-token would be: a new token once no window has been attached for 60 s, else 409 WINDOW_ATTACHED. A replayed transfer is R4's.

CODEX_NOT_READY's details.reason is a sentence in the endpoint table and the fixed word strict_file_rules_unproven in the safety-box rule. These fixtures use that word for unproven file rules and the state's reason sentence otherwise.

An invalid mode, like any malformed agent-session body (an unknown turn kind, settle next or interrupt reason, a missing field), is 422 INVALID_REQUEST_BODY since RAVIS's relay increment (R3). RAVIS's second increment (R2) fixed the rest of this family: a sign-in method other than browser is SIGN_IN_METHOD_NOT_SUPPORTED, a malformed Codex admin body is INVALID_REQUEST_BODY, and DELETE accept-version answers the full GET body.
GET /api/v1/codex/reprove returns the last result; only its state and result word are fixed.
The transcript's turn entries follow Codex's thread/turns/list summary view and are fixed against calibration's transcripts.

Decided by R3: the deltas_skipped marker is a frame with no id (so it never moves a cursor), event deltas_skipped, data {session_id, after: <the cursor>}, sent before the replayed events. A question's options are its labels as strings, and a window's answers map is {question id: answer text}. A normalised stream item carries its kind under type. The snapshot carries no list of recent completed items (the design's last 200): R3 follows these fixtures, and a window rebuilds progress from the settle's git reconciliation.

Decided by R3: a session settled with next: idle releases its project lock and its checkout lock file (lock: null), and a turn takes the lock back atomically; next: transfer keeps both, reserved for the destination's transfer token (R4 mints it); next: end archives the thread and releases.

Settled by calibration's harness (Cal): the shared lock rule is codex/lock_rule.py and the checkout lock file codex/lock_file.py. R3's project-lock seam is agent/locks.py and its process clean-up seam agent/cleanup.py; M29's fourth increment (R4) fills both.

Decided by R4: the checkout lock file's leftover entries are {pid, start, comm}, start as ps -o lstart= in the C locale (lock-rule-cases.json → lock_file_leftover). RAVIS writes the holding Codex session's recorded command processes there at each two-second look, and [] once they are confirmed gone. A window that finds a gone RAVIS holder may end exactly those, each by pid and start time, never by group.

Decided by R4: GET /api/v1/codex → account.fingerprint_sha256 is the current account's fingerprint, in the form SessionView → codex.account_fingerprint carries it, so a checkpoint's account can be compared with the current one. Named callers only; an anonymous reader doesn't get the field.

Decided by R4: every agent-session and project-lock route answers 503 CODEX_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE until a restart's reconciliation has run. Session create and turns answer 409 CODEX_NOT_READY {state: signed_in, reason: codex_update_pending} while a new Codex build waits to run, and a turn only waiting for an answer becomes paused_for_update ten minutes after the build appears.
Decided by R4: a replayed transfer returns the same transfer token within a RAVIS run, and a new one for the same live transfer after a restart (project-locks.json → decided_in_r4).
